title: No One Reached Me with This Step
text:
No one reached me with this step

of your slenderness in marble reflections.

Your blood bound to its bonds mirrors

of light images at random.


Crystal of blood whose light I pass through,

your body inflamed with reflections;

your body of circumflex reflections,

your dark body unfolded in satin.


I stretched my voice to the horizon placed

like bread in the sky of your absence.

Your arrival surrounds me, your voice, your gesture,


your cruelty, your sadness, and the terrible

certainty of being in your presence

full of love and inextinguishable death.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the marble-reflection imagery and the final fusion of love and inextinguishable death.

title: If Beside You the Hours Hurry
text:
If beside you the hours hurry

to remain in us forever,

today, when your sweet absence imprisons me,

I feel the dispersal of time at my heels

and in my ears and in my eyes.

I know no way to walk except toward you,

nor to hear any voice except that noble

voice that from the steaming edge of happiness

flies to tell me the words

that sharpened the water of the poem.


To say your name among living words

without anyone hearing it!

And to hear it only myself from the fine

silence of paper, in the half-light

left by the pencil, in the last

silent presences of the poem.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the beloved's name heard only in the paper-silence of the poem.

title: I Barely Know You and Already I Say to Myself...
text:
I barely know you and already I say to myself:

Will she never know that her person exalts

all in me that is blood and fire?


As if it were much

to wait a few days—many, few?—

because every hope

seems a South Sea, deep, long!

And because we are always

fruits of impatience, all forest.

I barely know you and already I razed

cities, clouds and landscape-journeys,

and astonished, I suddenly discover

that I am inside the present stone

and that in the sky there is not yet even a cloudlet.


What will these words be like, new,

when already beside you they fly out

and in the accent of your hands I see

the ineffable limit of space.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the impatience of new love and the startling image of being inside present stone.

title: Twilight Water, Thirsty Water...
text:
Twilight water, thirsty water,

the late birds leave you like syllables.

Swaying in the poplars, the wind subtracts from you

the happiness of your eyes drinking themselves in mine.

I allied my thought to your shadowy joys

and tasted the sweetness of your slow words.

You lengthened twilights in my thirsty hands:

I devoured your tragic summers in the bread.

My hands will remain moist from your breast.

From my stubbornness the poison will remain to you,

floating flower of anguish that destiny baptized.

From our two silences one day must spring

the luminous water that gives a divine blue

to the depth of cypresses of your soul and mine.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the water-silence sonnet and its final divine blue among cypresses.

title: To Juárez
text:
Sober with indigenous clay, the truth of your life.

It had a childhood of grain ears and ripened into maize.

You won your destiny for the lost sheep

and gave the trees a new root.


I see beside a lake your mended poverty

and the hand of day that gave you its varnish.

Justice on your lips consolidates its towers

and your solemnity has a happy air.


You are the lifetime President, despite

so much gloomy night. The Republic is a sea,

navigable and serene, if time consults you.


And if I can leave you now a wildflower,

it is because the people feel that in their adult hope

your faith will give them songs to await the dawn.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Pellicer's civic praise of Juárez as indigenous clay, maize, and navigable republic.

text:

editorial_note: This alternate-title variant keeps the same twilight-water sonnet and its luminous future water.

title: Come Closer...
text:
Come closer.

Beside the night I wait for you.


Swim me.

Deep and cold springs

stir my current alive.


See how pure my pools are.

What joy there is in my ice!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Conde's direct imperatives and water-body invitation.

title: Love
text:
Offering.


Come closer.

Beside the night I wait for you.

Swim me.


Deep and cold springs

stir my current alive.


See how pure my pools are.

What joy there is in my ice!
editorial_note: This titled variant preserves the embedded Offering heading and the same water invitation.

title: Conformity
text:
How much, Lord, I owe you for all the moments

when you could have made me suffer and did not!

The hours of pain add up to such slow times

that more than by age one grows old by sadness.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the grateful address to God and the aphoristic aging-by-sadness close.

title: You Were Falling into Me...
text:
You were falling into me.

Echo of your weight, my life

was a song rushing

into eternity.


Immersed in my silence,

you are the sky that holds up a stream,

that raises a tree.

In which a morning star cuts its voice

of eternity.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the falling beloved as weight, song, sky, stream, and star.
